record.paper_title: Open problems in microscopic theory of large-amplitude collective motion
record.original_question: When oblate and prolate Hartree-Fock-Bogoliubov shape minima coexist in the same nucleus without an exact discrete symmetry relating them, what are the correct collective degree or degrees of freedom that mediate the large-amplitude shape-mixing dynamics between those two configurations, and how can a microscopic theory identify and describe those coordinates?

evidence.quote: In this case, we do not know the relevant collective degree(s) of freedom through which the two shapes mix.
It is obviously needed to develop a microscopic theory capable of describing the shape mixing dynamics of this kind.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an atomic nucleus modeled by self-consistent mean-field (Hartree–Fock–Bogoliubov, HFB) theory whose energy surface, viewed as a function of intrinsic quadrupole deformation parameters (β, γ), possesses two distinct local minima: one of oblate shape and one of prolate shape. Assume that no exact discrete symmetry of the underlying nuclear Hamiltonian maps one minimum onto the other, so the two HFB configurations are genuinely inequivalent.

Develop a fully microscopic theory of large-amplitude collective motion that, starting solely from the nuclear many-body Hamiltonian and the HFB mean field, accomplishes the following:

(a) Identifies, in a non-empirical way, the correct collective degree (or degrees) of freedom — i.e., a collective subspace and corresponding collective coordinate(s) q on the manifold of HFB states — that mediate the large-amplitude shape-mixing dynamics between the oblate and prolate minima.

(b) Provides a constructive procedure (for instance, an extension of the adiabatic self-consistent collective coordinate method or equivalent) that determines the collective path / submanifold connecting the two minima together with the associated collective Hamiltonian, including its kinetic (inertial) functions and collective potential.

(c) Yields a quantization of this collective Hamiltonian whose eigenstates reproduce the observed shape-mixing spectroscopy (energy levels, E2 transition strengths, spectroscopic quadrupole moments) when no a priori symmetry relates the two coexisting shapes.

State precisely what the relevant collective coordinate(s) are in this generic asymmetric oblate–prolate coexistence situation and how they are to be extracted microscopically from the underlying many-body dynamics.
artifact.status_search_result: The adiabatic self-consistent collective coordinate (ASCC) method, together with local QRPA-derived inertial functions, has been applied successfully to oblate–prolate shape mixing (e.g., proton-rich Se isotopes, prolate–oblate transitions in the Er–Pt region), producing 5D quadrupole collective Hamiltonians that reproduce excitation spectra, B(E2) values, and spectroscopic quadrupole moments. These results give a microscopic identification of the (β, γ) collective coordinates as effective shape-mixing degrees of freedom in studied cases. However, a fully general microscopic prescription for the relevant collective coordinate(s) in arbitrary asymmetric coexistence situations (without symmetry relating the two minima) remains an active research problem rather than a fully closed one.

status_evidence.title: Microscopic description of oblate-prolate shape mixing in proton-rich Se isotopes
status_evidence.snippet: Oblate-prolate shape coexistence/mixing studied via the adiabatic self-consistent collective coordinate method, deriving the collective path and Hamiltonian microscopically.
status_evidence.claim: ASCC method has been applied to identify collective coordinates and describe oblate-prolate shape mixing microscopically.

status_evidence.title: Microscopic description of large-amplitude shape-mixing dynamics with inertial functions derived in local QRPA
status_evidence.snippet: Five-dimensional quadrupole collective Hamiltonian with inertial functions from local QRPA built on constrained HFB states reproduces shape-mixing spectroscopy.
status_evidence.claim: A microscopic framework producing inertial functions and collective Hamiltonian for shape-mixing dynamics has been developed.

status_evidence.title: Microscopic analysis of prolate-oblate shape phase transition and shape coexistence in the Er-Pt region
status_evidence.snippet: Prolate-oblate shape phase transition and coexistence analyzed microscopically in the Er–Pt region.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work continues to apply and extend microscopic shape-mixing theory, indicating ongoing development.
